enriched_description: Conical mountain formed by accumulated volcanic material with a central crater or vent at the summit. The surface exhibits dark, rough texture from solidified lava flows, volcanic ash, and pyroclastic deposits. Coloration ranges from black to dark gray with reddish-brown oxidized areas. The volcano profile shows steep slopes (30-35 degrees) with visible lava channels, fumaroles emitting steam, and sparse vegetation. Active volcanoes display glowing lava, smoke plumes, and ash clouds.

Athletic figure wearing a baseball uniform consisting of a button-front jersey with team insignia, matching pants with belt, cleated shoes, and a cap with a brim. The uniform exhibits team colors with visible numbering on the back. The player holds a leather baseball glove on one hand and may be in a batting, fielding, or pitching stance. Body posture shows athletic build with muscular arms and legs. Equipment includes a wooden or metal bat when batting.

Male figure dressed in formal wedding attire, typically wearing a dark suit or tuxedo with a white dress shirt, necktie or bow tie, and polished dress shoes. The outfit may include a boutonniere pinned to the lapel. The groom exhibits a well-groomed appearance with styled hair and a confident posture. Accessories may include a pocket square, cufflinks, and a wedding ring. The overall presentation is formal and ceremonial.

Underwater figure equipped with full scuba gear including a neoprene wetsuit (black or colored), buoyancy control device (BCD) vest, compressed air tank mounted on the back, regulator mouthpiece, mask covering eyes and nose, and fins on feet. The diver exhibits a horizontal swimming posture with arms extended or at sides. Equipment includes a pressure gauge, dive computer, and weight belt. Bubbles rise from the exhalation valve. The wetsuit shows a smooth, slightly reflective surface.

Small spherical seed with a smooth, hard outer shell in dark brown to black coloration, typically 1-2 mm in diameter. The surface exhibits a glossy finish with a slight sheen. Individual seeds are uniform in size and shape with a rounded, slightly flattened profile. When viewed in mass, the seeds form a dense, granular pile with a dark, uniform appearance. The seed coat is thin and brittle, revealing a pale yellow interior when cracked.

Composite flower with a central yellow disc surrounded by a single whorl of white ray petals (florets). The flower head measures 2-5 cm in diameter with 13-34 elongated white petals radiating outward from the bright yellow center. The petals are narrow, slightly pointed, and arranged in a flat, circular pattern. The flower is supported by a slender green stem with small alternate leaves. The center disc has a bumpy, granular texture from individual disc florets.

Distinctive orchid flower with a pouch-like yellow lip (labellum) resembling a slipper, surrounded by maroon to purple-brown sepals and petals. The inflated pouch measures 2-4 cm in length with a smooth, glossy yellow surface and subtle veining. The lateral petals are twisted and elongated, extending outward. The dorsal sepal arches over the pouch. The flower is supported by a hairy green stem with pleated basal leaves. Overall height 15-40 cm.

Dried grain kernels from the maize plant, exhibiting individual kernels that are flat to rounded with a hard, smooth outer pericarp. Color ranges from pale yellow to deep golden, with some varieties showing white, red, or multicolored kernels. Each kernel measures 5-10 mm with a characteristic cap-shaped profile and a visible germ spot at the base. In mass, the kernels form a granular pile with a matte, slightly dusty surface texture.

Nut fruit of the oak tree with a smooth, hard, brown shell (nut) seated in a woody, cup-shaped cap (cupule). The nut is ovoid to elliptical, typically 1.5-3 cm in length, with a glossy, dark brown surface and a pointed tip. The cupule covers one-quarter to one-half of the nut, exhibiting a rough, scaly texture with overlapping woody scales in light brown to gray coloration. The base shows a small attachment scar from the stem.

Small oval to round fruit of the rose plant, typically 1-2 cm in diameter, with a smooth, glossy surface in bright red to orange-red coloration. The fruit exhibits a slightly tapered shape with persistent dried sepals (calyx) at the apex forming a small crown. The surface is taut and shiny with subtle longitudinal striations. Cut cross-section reveals a hollow interior containing numerous small, hairy seeds (achenes) embedded in thin fleshy walls.
